newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude supported at $19.45, $19.25.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude supported at $19.45, $19.25.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20

+NYMEX crude is expected to find support first at $19.45 a barrel and then at $19.25 below that. Resistance is expected at $19.65 and then $19.85. +Gasoline faces resistance at 59.60-59.80 a gallon but a supportive trendline just below 58.00 will also provide support.
NYMEX crude oil futures are expected to open lower on Wednesday in line with fundamental-driven losses in London and dealers saw room for further losses.

August NYMEX crude oil closed 21 cents a barrel firmer on Tuesday at $19.73 a barrel while August gasoline was 0.98 cents up at 58.92 cents a gallon, and August heating oil gained 0.22 cents up at 53 cents.
Victor Yu at Refco said he saw support for crude first at $19.45 a barrel, the low point of Tuesday's session. Below that lies support at around $19.25.

This falls close to a support level at $19.29 cited by MeesPierson Derivatives in London, employing the Market Profile technique, as well as Friday's low of $19.28 - which is also the 50 percent retracement of the move from the $18.65 low on June 20 to the $20.39 high on July 2.
Yu also saw resistance at $19.65, the site of intraday resistance on Tuesday, and then at $19.80 a barrel, which was another level of intraday resistance beneath which the market stalled.
Brokers GNI said there was resistance on gasoline's spot month continuation chart, formed by the lows in early April.
"Solid resistance continues to block upside progress, but an uptrend line may be forming. Another successful test of the trend line could provide the incentive to buy," the company said.
The trend line shown in the company's daily report passes through the lows of June 25 and July 7 and crosses the price action just below 58.00 on Wednesday.
